candidates.name: Thames Barrier
candidates.story: Engineers used gates that rotate up from the riverbed to block storm surges while leaving navigation spans clear when open. The barrier became operational in 1982 and officially opened in 1984.
candidates.art_direction: Show a raised steel gate between two of the silver piers from a low river viewpoint so the gate profile is visible.

candidates.name: Forth Bridge
candidates.location: Firth of Forth, Scotland, United Kingdom
candidates.story: Crews extended cantilever arms in balance on both sides of the towers, then built the connecting suspended spans out from each side until the halves met. Jack-raised work platforms followed the growing struts and ties. The bridge was completed in November 1889 and formally opened on 4 March 1890; rail traffic began in March 1890.
candidates.art_direction: Depict balanced erection in the late 1880s: a great tubular steel tower with incomplete arms projecting on both sides, open gaps before the suspended spans join, granite piers and navigable water below. Make the two-sided balance the main readable silhouette. Use National Library of Scotland photographs and contemporary erection drawings to establish struts, ties and temporary jack-raised platforms before illustrating machinery. No modern cranes or suspension cables. Compose Frame landscape and portrait independently, reserving quiet upper-right sky. Grayscale crops must retain the tower and both growing arms. Unlike Millau deck launching and Golden Gate cable spinning, this story concerns self-supporting balanced cantilever erection.

candidates.name: Zollverein Shaft XII
candidates.story: Zollverein Shaft XII separated its load-bearing steel skeletons from lighter, non-load-bearing steel-grid curtain walls. The independent facade grids enclosed the industrial spaces while leaving the main structure adaptable to changing machinery. Construction ran from 1928 to 1932; the central shaft complex entered operation on 1 February 1932. This subject is the completed Shaft XII buildings, not the later coking plant.
candidates.art_direction: Show a Shaft XII industrial hall under construction around 1931: heavy internal steel columns and beams behind a lighter external steel facade grid, some grid bays still open and others filled with red brick and glazing. Make the separation of structure and enclosure clear in an interpretive open corner. Use Docomomo drawings and historical construction photographs before placing period lifting gear or workers. The double-bock headframe may appear as a contextual silhouette only after its erection date is verified. No modern escalator or later coking plant. Independently compose Frame orientations with quiet upper-right space; grayscale must distinguish the heavy frame from the thin facade grid. The story concerns industrial building construction, rather than mining decline or present-day reuse.
